items.headline: BioNTech adds clinical weight to its oncology pivot at WCLC 2026
items.preview: BioNTech presents promising oncology data at WCLC 2026, highlighting its evolving strategy.
items.article:
New data from the World Conference on Lung Cancer in Seoul are giving BioNTech’s oncology strategy more substance beyond its mRNA platform. Gotistobart has shown a marked survival benefit in previously treated squamous NSCLC, while the company’s leading bispecific antibody pumitamig continues to generate encouraging signals across tumor types and in combination with an antibody-drug conjugate.
Why this matters: A positive pivotal readout for gotistobart could provide BioNTech with a late-stage oncology asset independent of its mRNA cancer vaccine programs, addressing a significant unmet need in lung cancer treatment.
The latest evidence is coming from the World Conference on Lung Cancer (WCLC) in Seoul, where BioNTech is presenting clinical data from several stages of development. The most mature signal comes from gotistobart, an anti-CTLA-4 antibody being developed with US partner OncoC4. Meanwhile, longer-term data for the bispecific antibody pumitamig and early results from a pumitamig–ADC combination add further evidence that BioNTech is trying to build a broad, combination-driven oncology franchise.

items.headline: Human embryo base editing can reach all cells but causes unpredictable genetic changes
items.preview: Columbia University study reveals risks of gene editing in human embryos despite accuracy.
items.article:
A study by researchers at Columbia University Vagelos College of Physicians and Surgeons has found that new cutting-edge techniques can accurately edit genes in human embryos, but has also uncovered important risks that currently preclude the use of the techniques in the clinic. Editing the genome is essential for understanding human development, but the study highlights the unpredictable changes that can occur.
Why this matters: The findings indicate that while gene editing holds promise for preventing genetic disorders, the associated risks make it currently unsafe for clinical application.
The study used base editing to make changes in individual letters in the DNA of single-cell human embryos. While some experiments showed 100% successful editing, others resulted in unpredictable genetic changes, underscoring the need for caution in clinical applications.

items.headline: Carbon Dots Emerge as a Powerful Weapon Against Superbugs and Biofilms
items.preview: Review highlights carbon dots as promising antibacterial agents amid rising antibiotic resistance.
items.article:
A new comprehensive review published in the Journal of Nanoparticle Research surveys carbon dots, nanoscale carbon particles showing remarkable ability to kill bacteria and dismantle biofilms. As antibiotic resistance accelerates, these carbon-based nanomaterials are positioned as credible candidates for new antibacterial strategies.
Why this matters: Carbon dots could provide a novel approach to combat multidrug-resistant infections and biofilms, which are significant challenges in medical settings.
The review discusses how carbon dots generate reactive oxygen species to damage bacteria and disrupt biofilms, while also addressing the challenges of consistency in production and long-term biocompatibility.

items.headline: Hidden RNA Circles Help Rice Survive Heat and Drought Together
items.preview: Study reveals circular RNAs play a role in rice's response to combined heat and drought stress.
items.article:
A new study published in Molecular Genetics and Genomics has mapped a layer of gene regulation in rice involving circular RNAs (circRNAs) that help the plant respond to simultaneous heat and drought stress. This research highlights the complexity of plant stress responses and the potential for circRNAs to serve as targets for crop improvement.
Why this matters: Understanding circRNA-mediated regulation could lead to enhanced resilience in rice, crucial for food security amid climate change.
The study identified 208 high-confidence circRNAs and suggested that they are involved in critical processes like protein folding and nutrient mobilization, indicating their importance in stress tolerance.

items.headline: With pharmaceutical tariffs looming, guidance on compliance is still lacking
items.preview: Upcoming pharmaceutical tariffs raise concerns over compliance and impact on biotech innovation.
items.article:
With tariffs on patented pharmaceuticals set to take effect on Sept. 29, the lack of clarity about rules and exemptions complicates business decisions for biotech firms. These tariffs could reduce funds for developing treatments and threaten patient access to drugs.
Why this matters: The uncertainty surrounding these tariffs may deter investment in biotech and hinder innovation, impacting the availability of new therapies for patients.
The Biotechnology Innovation Organization (BIO) is seeking guidance on compliance and potential exemptions, but much of the necessary federal guidance remains missing as the implementation date approaches.
